title: fix(app-shell): Studio's nav-item inspector shows a locale-map label and edits only the designer locale's entry (objectui#11148)
body:
Fixes #11148
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

`StudioNavItemInspector` (the Studio Interfaces pillar's right-panel editor for the selected nav item) read the label as `String(node.label ?? node.title ?? node.name ?? '')`. A nav item's `label` is an `I18nLabel`, a plain string or an inline locale map, so a map showed as `[object Object]`. The Label input wrote `patch({ label: e.target.value })`, so the first keystroke replaced the whole map with one string and deleted every other language's text. The canvas card beside it already keeps the map since PR objectui#11146 (objectui#11128); this is the same rule on the second editor of the same label.

## What changed

- New internal module `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/navItemLabel.ts`, not exported from the package root. It holds both halves, so the two editors of one label cannot disagree:
  - `navItemLabelText(label, locale)`: the label's text in the designer locale, through the spec's `resolveI18nLabel`, or `''` when there is none. It is not trimmed, so an input bound to it echoes what the author typed.
  - `renamedLabel(cur, next, locale)`: moved verbatim out of `AppNavCanvas.tsx`, where it was module-private. The key choice (exact tag, else bare language, else a new exact-tag entry) now has one copy.
- `AppNavCanvas.tsx`: imports both. `navLabel` keeps its trim and its positional fallback, over `navItemLabelText`. No behaviour change.
- `StudioDesignSurface.tsx`, `StudioNavItemInspector` only:
  - display: `curLabel` is `navItemLabelText(label, locale)`, in the designer locale from `useMetadataLocale()` (the hook the inspector already called, and the one the canvas calls). `title` / `name` are no longer read;
  - edit: the Label input writes `renamedLabel(label, typed text, locale)`;
  - the placeholder check (`isPlaceholder`) keeps its semantics, on the resolved text;
  - object binding: see Acceptance notes.
- One changeset, `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`.

## Pins

New file `StudioDesignSurface.navItemInspectorLabelMaps-11148.test.tsx`, 8 tests, rendering the real inspector under `I18nProvider` in en and in zh:

- a map label shows its resolved text under en (`Accounts`) and under zh (`客户`), never `[object Object]`;
- `title` / `name` are not read as the label;
- an edit under zh changes only `zh-CN`, and `en` survives;
- an edit under en writes the `en` entry the input read, not a second `en-US` key;
- a map with no designer-locale entry gains one exactly once over three keystrokes (a stateful harness feeds each patch back, the way `InterfacesPillar` holds the draft), and the input shows the typed text;
- a plain-string label edits to a plain string, as before (the control);
- binding an object keeps a real map label as authored, and the item still parses under `NavigationItemSchema`.

PR objectui#11146's canvas pins (`AppNavCanvas.labelMaps-11128.test.tsx`) are unchanged and green, as are the objectui#4881 inspector pins.

## Ablation

One-off, after the fix was committed at `575bbb6e6`. Each leg reverts one site to its `origin/main` spelling through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode (anchor hit 1 to 0, replacement 0 to 1, blob changed), runs the new file, and restores; each restore is proven by the file's blob equal to the HEAD blob and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

| leg | site reverted | new file |
|---|---|---|
| A1 display | `curLabel` back to `String(node.label ?? node.title ?? node.name ?? '')` | 4 failed, 4 passed |
| A2 edit | Label input back to `patch({ label: e.target.value })` | 3 failed, 5 passed |
| A3 bind | bind back to `isPlaceholder && obj ? obj.label : curLabel` | 1 failed, 7 passed |

At HEAD the file is 8 passed.

## Gates

All at HEAD `575bbb6e6` unless stated.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/`: Test Files 153 passed (153), Tests 1505 passed (1505).
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/studio-locale.i18n.test.tsx`, the other test that imports `AppNavCanvas` outside those directories: 5 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`), after `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^...` (28 of 28 tasks successful): exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists both the new test and the new module.
- eslint on the 4 changed files: exit 0, 0 errors and 20 warnings as the package's own `eslint .` sees them. Per-rule counts on the two edited files are identical at base and at head, with and without `--no-inline-config`. Population: the four changed files, all inside the `@object-ui/app-shell` lint target. `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. `check:control-bytes`: exit 0. `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations, exit 0. `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:i18n-keys`: exit 0.
- Declared narrowing: the full `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint` farm is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **Object binding.** The dispatch asked that `curLabel`'s semantics be kept, on the resolved text, at the site where binding an object writes the label. Read literally, the bind would write the resolved text (a string) over a map label, which is this card's defect through another door: ablation leg A3 is that literal reading, and it turns the bind pin red. The bind now keeps a real label as authored, and on a placeholder item it adopts the object's label through `renamedLabel`. A plain-string placeholder therefore still becomes the object's label exactly as before.
- **One entry per keystroke** (the dispatch's mechanism check): measured. Under zh-CN a map with only `en` gains `zh-CN` on the first keystroke, and every later keystroke finds that entry first; the pin asserts the key list after each of three keystrokes.
- **Reported to the seat, not changed here.** A probe (uncommitted, deleted) rendered the real `InterfacesPillar` with a map-labelled nav item: the pillar's left rail renders a nav item's `label` raw, React throws `Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {en, zh-CN})`, and neither nav entry renders. The same harness with a plain-string label renders the rail. `resolveSurface` in `navSurface.ts` also stringifies the label into the canvas title. Details and dedupe words are in the dev report on the card.
- Several comments in this area still name an `AppNavInspector` component that no longer exists in the tree. Not touched.
